```{r}
# ============================================================
# Biomass allocation — flexible single-df version
# Works with partial data (not all 12 cells required)
# ============================================================

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
```


```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. CONFIGURATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------

PERIOD_PLOT <- 2045
REGION_PLOT <- "DEU"
PLOT_MODE   <- "grid"        # "grid" | "individual" | "both"
PLOT_MODE_ABS <- "grid"   # "grid" | "individual" | "both" | "none"
UNIT_LABEL    <- "EJ/yr"  # adjust to your unit
EXPORT_DIR  <- "."
```


```{r}
tot   <- "PE|Biomass"
items <- c(
  "PE|Biomass|Solids",
  "PE|Biomass|Liquids",
  "PE|Biomass|Gases",
  "PE|Biomass|Heat",
  "PE|Biomass|Electricity",
  "PE|Biomass|Biochar"
)

fraction_labels <- c(
  "PE|Biomass|Solids"      = "Solids",
  "PE|Biomass|Liquids"     = "Liquids",
  "PE|Biomass|Gases"       = "Gases",
  "PE|Biomass|Heat"        = "Heat",
  "PE|Biomass|Electricity" = "Electricity",
  "PE|Biomass|Biochar"     = "Biochar"
)

fraction_colors <- c(
  "Solids"      = "#7F77DD",
  "Liquids"     = "#1D9E75",
  "Gases"       = "#3B8BD4",
  "Heat"        = "#E8593C",
  "Electricity" = "#EF9F27",
  "Biochar"     = "#888780"
)

bio_levels <- c("BAU", "Low", "Stable", "High")
ccs_levels <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")
```


```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. INPUT — replace with your actual dataframe
# Expected extra columns: bio_avail, ccs_avail
# (add these when binding your dfs, or derive from scenario)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df_input <- bind_rows(
#   bBAU_ccsLow    |> mutate(bio_avail = "BAU",    ccs_avail = "Low"),
  bBAU_ccsMedium |> mutate(bio_avail = "BAU",    ccs_avail = "Medium"),
#   bBAU_ccsHigh   |> mutate(bio_avail = "BAU",    ccs_avail = "High"),
#   bLow_ccsLow    |> mutate(bio_avail = "Low",    ccs_avail = "Low"),
#   bLow_ccsMedium |> mutate(bio_avail = "Low",    ccs_avail = "Medium"),
#   bLow_ccsHigh   |> mutate(bio_avail = "Low",    ccs_avail = "High"),
#   bStable_ccsLow    |> mutate(bio_avail = "Stable", ccs_avail = "Low"),
#   bStable_ccsMedium |> mutate(bio_avail = "Stable", ccs_avail = "Medium"),
  bStable_ccsHigh   |> mutate(bio_avail = "Stable", ccs_avail = "High"),
#   bHigh_ccsLow    |> mutate(bio_avail = "High",  ccs_avail = "Low"),
  bHigh_ccsMedium |> mutate(bio_avail = "High",  ccs_avail = "Medium"),
  bHigh_ccsHigh   |> mutate(bio_avail = "High",  ccs_avail = "High")
)   # <-- add this line   # <-- swap to your single df here

# If bio_avail / ccs_avail are not yet columns, derive them
# from the dataframe name or add them manually, e.g.:
# df_input <- df_input |> mutate(bio_avail = "Low", ccs_avail = "High")
```


```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. FILTER & COMPUTE SHARES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df_plot <- df_input |>
  filter(
    region   == REGION_PLOT,
    period   == PERIOD_PLOT,
    variable %in% c(tot, items)
  ) |>
  group_by(bio_avail, ccs_avail) |>
  filter(scenario == first(unique(scenario))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(bio_avail, ccs_avail, variable, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(items),
    names_to  = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share     = value / .data[[tot]],
    fraction  = factor(fraction_labels[variable], levels = names(fraction_colors)),
    # Factor levels include full set so grid stays consistent
    # as data arrives; missing cells simply render empty
    bio_avail = factor(bio_avail, levels = bio_levels),
    ccs_avail = factor(ccs_avail, levels = ccs_levels)
  )

# Detect which cells actually have data — useful for messaging
cells_present <- df_plot |>
  distinct(bio_avail, ccs_avail) |>
  mutate(label = paste0("b", bio_avail, "_ccs", ccs_avail))

message("Cells with data: ", paste(cells_present$label, collapse = ", "))
```


```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. SHARED THEME & SCALE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

theme_biomass <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid        = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing     = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "grey85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
      strip.text.x      = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30", margin = margin(b = 4)),
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30", angle = 0, hjust = 1,
                                       margin = margin(r = 6)),
      strip.placement   = "outside",
      strip.background  = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x       = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks        = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x      = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", margin = margin(t = 8)),
      axis.title.y      = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", margin = margin(r = 8)),
      legend.position   = "right",
      legend.title      = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.text       = element_text(size = 8.5),
      plot.title        = element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey15", margin = margin(b = 3)),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "grey45", margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.caption      = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey55", hjust = 0),
      plot.margin       = margin(12, 12, 10, 12)
    )
}

scale_fill_biomass <- function() {
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fraction_colors,
    name   = "Output fraction",
    guide  = guide_legend(keywidth = unit(0.4, "cm"), keyheight = unit(0.4, "cm"), ncol = 1)
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5a. GRID PLOT
# Empty cells render as blank panels — placeholder for
# data still to come. Switch drop = FALSE keeps the full
# 4×3 grid intact regardless of how many cells have data.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_grid_plot <- function() {
  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = "", y = share, fill = fraction)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
    facet_grid(
      rows     = vars(ccs_avail),
      cols     = vars(bio_avail),
      labeller = labeller(
        ccs_avail = c(Low    = "Low CCS",
                      Medium = "Medium CCS",
                      High   = "High CCS"),
        bio_avail = c(BAU    = "BAU biomass",
                      Low    = "Low biomass",
                      Medium = "Medium biomass",
                      High   = "High biomass")
      ),
      switch = "y",
      drop   = FALSE             # keeps empty cells in the grid
    ) +
    scale_fill_biomass() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
      expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1)
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = "Biomass allocation across sensitivity scenarios",
      subtitle = paste0("Germany \u00b7 ", PERIOD_PLOT,
                        " \u00b7 Rows = CCS availability \u00b7 Columns = biomass availability"),
      x        = "Biomass availability \u2192",
      y        = "CCS availability \u2192",
      caption  = paste0("Region: ", REGION_PLOT,
                        " \u00b7 Cells with data: ",
                        paste(cells_present$label, collapse = ", "))
    ) +
    theme_biomass()
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5b. INDIVIDUAL PLOTS — only for cells that have data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_individual_plot <- function(bio, ccs) {
  df_cell <- df_plot |> filter(bio_avail == bio, ccs_avail == ccs)

  ggplot(df_cell, aes(x = "", y = share, fill = fraction)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_biomass() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
      expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1)
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = paste0(bio, " biomass \u00b7 ", ccs, " CCS"),
      subtitle = paste0("Germany \u00b7 ", PERIOD_PLOT),
      x        = NULL,
      y        = "Share of total biomass",
      caption  = paste("Region:", REGION_PLOT,
                       "\u00b7 PE|Biomass fractions as share of PE|Biomass")
    ) +
    theme_biomass(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", margin = margin(r = 6)),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40")
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5c. GRID PLOT — absolute values
# ------------------------------------------------------------
make_grid_plot_abs <- function() {
  y_max <- df_plot |>
  group_by(bio_avail, ccs_avail) |>
  summarise(total = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pull(total) |>
  max(na.rm = TRUE)

  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = "", y = value, fill = fraction)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
    facet_grid(
      rows     = vars(ccs_avail),
      cols     = vars(bio_avail),
      labeller = labeller(
        ccs_avail = c(Low    = "Low CCS",
                      Medium = "Medium CCS",
                      High   = "High CCS"),
        bio_avail = c(BAU    = "BAU biomass",
                      Low    = "Low biomass",
                      Stable = "Stable biomass",
                      High   = "High biomass")
      ),
      switch = "y",
      drop   = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_biomass() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = c(0, 0),
      limits = c(0, y_max * 1.05),   # 5% headroom
      name   = UNIT_LABEL
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = "Biomass allocation across sensitivity scenarios (absolute)",
      subtitle = paste0("Germany \u00b7 ", PERIOD_PLOT,
                        " \u00b7 Rows = CCS availability \u00b7 Columns = biomass availability"),
      x        = "Biomass availability \u2192",
      y        = paste0("CCS availability \u2192"),
      caption  = paste0("Region: ", REGION_PLOT,
                        " \u00b7 Unit: ", UNIT_LABEL,
                        " \u00b7 Cells with data: ",
                        paste(cells_present$label, collapse = ", "))
    ) +
    theme_biomass() +
    theme(
      # show y-axis text so values are readable across cells
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey40"),
      axis.ticks.y = element_line(colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3)
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5d. INDIVIDUAL PLOTS — absolute values
# ------------------------------------------------------------
make_individual_plot_abs <- function(bio, ccs) {
  df_cell <- df_plot |> filter(bio_avail == bio, ccs_avail == ccs)
  y_max <- df_plot |>
  group_by(bio_avail, ccs_avail) |>
  
  summarise(total = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pull(total) |>
  max(na.rm = TRUE)
  ggplot(df_cell, aes(x = "", y = value, fill = fraction)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_biomass() +
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = c(0, 0),
      limits = c(0, y_max * 1.05)
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = paste0(bio, " biomass \u00b7 ", ccs, " CCS"),
      subtitle = paste0("Germany \u00b7 ", PERIOD_PLOT),
      x        = NULL,
      y        = UNIT_LABEL,
      caption  = paste("Region:", REGION_PLOT,
                       "\u00b7 Unit:", UNIT_LABEL)
    ) +
    theme_biomass(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", margin = margin(r = 6)),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40"),
      axis.ticks.y = element_line(colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3)
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. RENDER & EXPORT
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (PLOT_MODE %in% c("grid", "both")) {
  p_grid <- make_grid_plot()
  print(p_grid)

#   ggsave(
#     file.path(EXPORT_DIR, paste0("biomass_allocation_", PERIOD_PLOT, "_grid.pdf")),
#     plot = p_grid, width = 200, height = 140, units = "mm", device = cairo_pdf
#   )
#   ggsave(

#     plot = p_grid, width = 200, height = 140, units = "mm", dpi = 300
#   )
#   message("Saved: grid plot")
}

if (PLOT_MODE %in% c("individual", "both")) {
  # Only iterate over cells that actually have data
  pwalk(cells_present, function(bio_avail, ccs_avail, label) {
    p <- make_individual_plot(bio_avail, ccs_avail)
    print(p)

    # ggsave(
    #   file.path(EXPORT_DIR, paste0("biomass_allocation_", PERIOD_PLOT, "_", label, ".pdf")),

    # message("Saved: ", label)

}

# Absolute plots
if (PLOT_MODE_ABS %in% c("grid", "both")) {
  p_grid_abs <- make_grid_plot_abs()
  print(p_grid_abs)
  # ggsave(file.path(EXPORT_DIR, paste0("biomass_allocation_", PERIOD_PLOT, "_grid_abs.pdf")),
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. FILTER & COMPUTE SHARES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df_plot <- df_all |>
  filter(
    region   == REGION_PLOT,
    period   == PERIOD_PLOT,
    variable %in% c(tot, items)
  ) |>
  # keep only the first scenario per cell if multiple exist;
  # replace with filter(scenario == "your_scenario") if needed
  group_by(bio_avail, ccs_avail) |>
  filter(scenario == first(unique(scenario))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(bio_avail, ccs_avail, variable, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(items),
    names_to  = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share     = value / .data[[tot]],
    fraction  = fraction_labels[variable],
    fraction  = factor(fraction, levels = names(fraction_colors)),
    bio_avail = factor(bio_avail, levels = bio_levels),
    ccs_avail = factor(ccs_avail, levels = ccs_levels)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. PLOT
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = "", y = share, fill = fraction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  facet_grid(
    rows     = vars(ccs_avail),
    cols     = vars(bio_avail),
    labeller = labeller(
      ccs_avail = c(Low    = "Low CCS",
                    Medium = "Medium CCS",
                    High   = "High CCS"),
      bio_avail = c(BAU    = "BAU biomass",
                    Low    = "Low biomass",
                    Medium = "Medium biomass",
                    High   = "High biomass")
    ),
    switch = "y"
  ) +
  # Vertical separator to visually isolate BAU from the
  # Low/Medium/High gradient. Draws a line after column 1.
  geom_vline(
    data        = df_plot |> filter(bio_avail == "Low", ccs_avail == "Low"),
    aes(xintercept = 1.5),
    colour      = "grey50",
    linewidth   = 0.4,
    linetype    = "dashed",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fraction_colors,
    name   = "Output fraction",
    guide  = guide_legend(keywidth = unit(0.4, "cm"), keyheight = unit(0.4, "cm"), ncol = 1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Biomass allocation across sensitivity scenarios",
    subtitle = paste0("Germany \u00b7 ", PERIOD_PLOT,
                      " \u00b7 Rows = CCS availability \u00b7 Columns = biomass availability"),
    x        = "Biomass availability \u2192",
    y        = "CCS availability \u2192",
    caption  = paste("Region:", REGION_PLOT,
                     "\u00b7 PE|Biomass fractions as share of total primary biomass energy",
                     "\u00b7 Dashed line separates BAU from sensitivity range")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing     = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "grey85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.text.x      = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30", angle = 0, hjust = 1,
                                     margin = margin(r = 6)),
    strip.placement   = "outside",
    strip.background  = element_blank(),
    # Highlight BAU strip label to visually distinguish it
    strip.text.x.top  = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    axis.text         = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks        = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x      = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", margin = margin(t = 8)),
    axis.title.y      = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", margin = margin(r = 8)),
    legend.position   = "right",
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 8.5),
    plot.title        = element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey15", margin = margin(b = 3)),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "grey45", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey55", hjust = 0),
    plot.margin       = margin(12, 12, 10, 12)
  )

print(p)
```
